name: Hash-Seed Serialization Divergence
essence: A cache key built by iterating an unordered set differs each process, because the hash seed is randomized -- so the cache never hits and 'it works on my machine.'

examples.summary: Set iteration depends on the process hash seed, so equivalent tag sets generate incompatible cache keys across workers..
examples.mechanism: Set iteration depends on the process hash seed, so equivalent tag sets generate incompatible cache keys across workers.

ingredients.suggests: Catalog key generation depends on process hash state through set iteration.
The same tags produce different cache keys in two workers.

examples.summary: Unspecified map traversal produces a different cache key for unchanged tags.
examples.mechanism: Unspecified map traversal produces a different cache key for unchanged tags.

ingredients.suggests: Key construction depends on randomized map traversal.
The cache indexes unchanged content by an unstable serialized key.

examples.summary: Identical catalog tags fail to reuse the cache entry.
examples.mechanism: The key function depends on a newly randomized HashSet iteration order. Equivalent tag sets produce keys that fail to find the stored catalog entry.
